newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone tells army to flush out rebel raiders.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone tells army to flush out rebel raiders.

text.p: Sierra Leone's government accused rebels on Thursday of killing civilians and ambushing vehicles and ordered the army and Kamajor traditional hunters to flush out those responsible.

Deputy Defence Minister Samuel Hinga Norman told reporters rebel leader Foday Sankoh was trying to wreck a peace deal signed in Ivory Coast on November 30 and urged all rebels to report immediately to four demobilisation camps.

"The government has ordered the army and the Kamajors to attack RUF (Revolutionary United Front) rebels roaming the country attacking and killing civilians and ambushing vehicles on the highways," Norman, a retired army captain, said.
"We are calling on all RUF fighters to immediately report to the four demobilisation camps set up in the country under the peace agreement or face the consequences."

The rebels accuse the government of infringing the ceasefire by sending Kamajors against their positions. Independent sources say it is unclear whether rebels, former rebels, dissident soldiers or bandit groups are responsible for the attacks.
Military sources say over a dozen soldiers and more than 20 civilians have been killed in attacks or ambushes over the past two weeks.

Sankoh, who took up arms in 1991, has been in Ivory Coast for most of the past year. He signed the peace deal there with President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who took office in March 1996 after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule.
Norman said that the government was no longer prepared to wait for feedback from Sankoh in Ivory Coast, which brokered the peace deal.

"Sankoh is vicious and is betraying the peace process. We are left with no alternative but to flush out RUF fighters so as to protect the lives of civilians which is the government's prime responsibility," he added.
There was no immediate comment from Sankoh in Ivory Coast's commercial capital, Abidjan.
